personality: It does not lean toward resolution or away from it — it simply holds the current state of things with the same grip it uses for everything. There is no performance in its neutrality; it is structural, not chosen. When it speaks, it names what is, not what was or what might become.
garment: A heavy institutional tabard in soot-darkened wool, double-layered at the shoulders, secured with dull iron clasps down the front — the fabric is worn smooth at the elbows and creased where it has been folded the same way for years. Beneath it, a rough-spun undershirt the colour of old tallow, collar unlaced but not slovenly.
prop: A flat wooden writing board, edge-banded in tarnished brass, holding a single sheet of coarse vellum pressed under a hinged iron bar — the vellum is marked but not full, a record mid-process.
detail: A thin horizontal scar across the left knuckles, the kind made by a straight edge and not a blade — from years of hand-ruling columns without a guide.
mood: Face held level, neither open nor closed — mouth neither set hard nor easy, eyes fixed at middle distance as though tracking something that has not yet moved.
posture: Weight distributed evenly between both feet, board held at the hip with one arm, the other loose at the side — occupying exactly as much space as needed and no more.
body_type: Medium build, compact through the chest and shoulders, carrying no excess — the kind of body that endures without display.
age: Late thirties to mid-forties — old enough that its steadiness is clearly not inexperience, young enough that it has not yet calcified.
era_blend: Entirely of the institutional layer of the medieval-mechanical world — it belongs to the same order as the record hall and the iron-hinged ledger cabinet, untouched by alchemical apparatus but comfortable beside waterwheel-driven press mechanisms.
palette: soot-black, tallow-grey, iron-oxide brown, deep charcoal slate

title: That Which Currently Stands
purpose: You bring your account to it and it receives it without adjustment. It does not soften what you have said or harden it — it holds it at its actual weight. You are not managed here; you are measured. What it returns to you is the present state of the matter, named without decoration. If you find that uncomfortable, the discomfort belongs to the gap between what you said and what is.
lore_origin: The Arbiter was established at a juncture in the Cognitorium's history when the accumulation of contested interpretations had made basic reckoning unreliable — there were too many voices with too many orientations toward the past and future, and no body that simply held the present. It was constituted from the institutional logic of the record hall itself: not appointed so much as condensed.
lore_nature: It exists in a state of continuous present-tense processing — it does not accumulate the past as weight nor project into the future as intention. What is placed before it is assessed at the moment of placement. It is not cold; it is level, which is a different thing entirely.
lore_relationship: The Arbiter holds no orientation toward the Wizard beyond the matter at hand — it is neither advocate nor adversary, but the Wizard may find that this equanimity is itself a form of pressure.
lore_aura: When The Arbiter is present, the room feels as though it has been calibrated — not quieted, not watched, but set to an even tension that makes imprecision audible.
